description: LayerX Image Inspector - open-source terminal explorer for container images. Browse layers, spot wasted bytes, and gate CI on image efficiency. Works with Docker, Podman, and OCI archives from a single static binary.

summary.one_liner: LayerX Image Inspector is an open-source terminal tool (Go) for browsing container image layers, finding wasted bytes, comparing two images, and gating CI on image efficiency, with support for Docker, Podman, and OCI/docker-save archives.
summary.what_it_does: LayerX opens a container image in an interactive TUI and shows a per-layer file tree with added, modified, and removed files colour-coded. It lets you view file contents, extract files from any layer, sort and filter by size or name, and jump to the layer responsible for the most wasted bytes. It reads live images via the Docker or Podman API, or reads docker save, podman save, and OCI-layout archives directly from disk without a daemon. The `layerx ci` subcommand checks efficiency, wasted-byte, and path rules from flags or a .layerx.yaml file and returns pass/fail exit codes. The `layerx compare` subcommand reports size, efficiency, and file deltas between two images in text, JSON, or Markdown, and `--json` exports the full analysis. The README also describes a set of colour themes and a local analysis cache.
use_cases: debug a bloated Docker image and find the RUN step responsible
gate a CI build on image efficiency or wasted bytes
compare two image releases for size and file changes
inspect an image tarball on an airgapped machine without a daemon
browse and extract files from a container image layer
review a Dockerfile change's filesystem impact before shipping
notable: Works with live Docker and Podman engines and with docker save / OCI-layout archives read directly from disk, with no daemon needed
layerx ci exits 0/1/2 for pass, rule failure, and operational error, so it can gate a pipeline
layerx compare reports size, efficiency, and file deltas between two images, with text, JSON, or Markdown output
Signed releases with SPDX SBOMs and SLSA Build Level 3 provenance; a Container image is also published to GHCR
Eight built-in TUI colour themes and a --platform flag for selecting a specific image variant
caveats: Live image inspection needs a running Docker or Podman engine; archive mode is the daemon-free alternative
The container image needs the host engine socket bind-mounted and, on Linux with Docker, a group-add step for the root:docker socket
The README lists macOS 13 Ventura or later as the supported macOS version and says Go 1.27.3+ is required to build from source
